ping.summary: Send ICMP echo requests to see whether a host answers and how long replies take.
flags: stop after N requests (without it the simulator sends 4, then prints ^C)
seconds to wait for each reply
ping.note: No reply does not mean the host is down: firewalls often drop ICMP, so a ping sweep can undercount.

flags: milliseconds to wait for each reply
windows.note: No reply does not mean the host is down: firewalls often drop ICMP, so a ping sweep can undercount. Note that Windows counts "Destination host unreachable" replies from your own address as received.

netstat.summary: The older tool for the same job as ss.
netstat.note: Many systems now ship ss instead of netstat; the information is the same.

windows.summary: List the connections and listening ports of this workstation, with the owning process id.
flags: all: listening ports as well as established connections
add the PID column: the process that owns the socket
windows.note: State LISTENING with foreign address 0.0.0.0:0 is a service waiting for connections; 0.0.0.0 in the local address means every interface, 127.0.0.1 only this machine. -b (program names) needs an administrator and is refused.

nslookup.summary: A quick name lookup: the server asked, then the answer (one question per command here).
flags: an address is looked up in reverse (PTR)
the address of the name server to ask
nslookup.note: A name without a dot gets the search domain added first (web-03 becomes web-03.corp.local). Interactive mode is not available in the simulator.

windows.note: On Windows the server is shown by its name. A name without a dot gets the search domain added first. Interactive mode is not available in the simulator.

curl.summary: Fetch a web page, or just its headers, and see what the server announces about itself.
flags: send HEAD and show only the response headers
show the headers and then the page
silent: no error messages (-S shows them again)
give up connecting after s seconds
curl.note: Headers such as Server and X-Powered-By tell an attacker the software and its version. Plain http only: https, -L (follow redirects) and -v are not simulated.

ipconfig.summary: Show this workstation's network settings: address, mask, gateway, DNS servers, MAC.
flags: address, subnet mask and default gateway of each adapter
adds host name, physical (MAC) address, DHCP details and DNS servers
ipconfig.note: The Windows counterpart of ip addr and ip route. /release, /renew and /flushdns change the system and are not available in the simulator.

findstr.summary: Search text for lines containing a word (the Windows grep).
flags: print the lines that do NOT match
findstr.note: Use it behind a pipe: netstat -ano | findstr 3389. Several words separated by spaces match any of them. Searches are literal in the simulator.

type.note: The Windows counterpart of cat. It reads the workstation's own files only.
